info.title: Surla MCP Software Factory Control Plane
info.description: The Surla project server: coding agents propose, build, test and verify changes to a Goa and Goa-AI service through its MCP tools, and the user agrees each change and approves its result on its views page.

get.description: List the builder's assignment for the project's open build while that role has work; empty otherwise. Reading the list records nothing and moves no working copy.

403.description: forbidden: The authenticated caller may not perform this operation or does not own the resource.

get.description: Return the builder's assignment for the open build's change in full and record that the builder read it at its revision. The first read of a new build joins the builder's working copy to the build's own branch, surla/build-<n> at the build's base: a copy with uncommitted work on an earlier build branch first gets that work committed there with the message "Left uncommitted when change <change_id> started"; a copy with nothing uncommitted joins from any branch. A copy with uncommitted work on any other branch, or a Git operation in progress, is refused with copy_off_branch, and a copy whose turn is held with working_copy_busy; nothing is marked read then. Building the change again makes the assignment unread.

403.description: forbidden: The authenticated caller may not perform this operation or does not own the resource.

404.description: not_found: You have no build assignment for this change_id: it is not the change of the project's open build.

409.description:
no_build: The user dropped this change's build: stop work on it and make no more edits or commits for it. The user starts builds on the views page.

copy_off_branch: Your working copy cannot join the build: it holds uncommitted work on a branch that is not an earlier build branch, or a Git operation is in progress. The message states the facts and the goal; put your work right with git, then read the assignment again.

working_copy_busy: Surla is starting a build in your working folder, or files there changed while Surla moved it (nothing was lost); call get_builder_assignment again.

working_folder_missing: Your working folder is missing; ask the user to build this change again on the views page.

get.description: List the test writer's assignment for the project's open build while that role has work; empty otherwise. Reading the list records nothing and moves no working copy.

403.description: forbidden: The authenticated caller may not perform this operation or does not own the resource.

get.description: Return the test writer's assignment for a change in full (the working folder, the design and Story as agreed at the built revision, the user's confirmed answers, confirmation examples and preserved behaviors of that revision, the tests it requires, and the state with the text of any findings) and record that the test writer read it at its revision. Later revisions do not change what the build saved. A new build of the change replaces the assignment, which then counts as unread, and so does each verdict of Surla's check. The first read of a new build joins your working copy to the build's branch, surla/tests-<n> at the build's base. A read that marks the assignment read also writes the required tests' generated folder into your copy. A copy with uncommitted work on an earlier tests build branch first gets that work committed there; a clean copy joins from any branch. Other uncommitted work or a Git operation is refused with copy_off_branch; nothing is marked read then.

403.description: forbidden: The authenticated caller may not perform this operation or does not own the resource.

404.description: not_found: You have no test assignment for this change_id.

409.description:
no_build: The user dropped this change's build: stop work on it and make no more edits or commits for it. The user starts builds on the views page.

copy_off_branch: Your working copy cannot join or serve this build: the message states its branch, the build's branch, any Git operation and what is uncommitted, and the goal. Put your test files on the build's branch, uncommitted, because Surla commits what it accepts; then call again.

working_copy_busy: Surla is checking the tests in your working folder; call get_test_writer_assignment again when the check has ended.

working_folder_missing: Your working folder is missing; ask the user to build this change again on the views page.

post.description: The test writer reports that its tests for a change at the build's revision are finished. Every report raises the build's report number by one and makes the state reported, from any state, clearing an earlier verdict, and returns at once. Surla then checks the tests in the working folder against the build's Story; its verdict, needs_changes, accepted or could_not_run, replaces reported in the test writer's assignment, which then counts as unread. A report for another revision, or in a project with stored verification settings, where no test writer is used, is refused and changes nothing.

get.description: Return the current change list's version as soon as it differs from since, the version of the list the caller last read, or after a bounded wait of a few seconds when nothing changed. The version also changes when the owner's Story evaluation starts, finishes or is replaced, or a public fact in get_team changes. The views page keeps one such read open and, only when the version changed, calls list_changes again and, while it shows the Story, get_story_refresh. Each call is traced but never saved in the diagnostics history list_traces reads, so an open page does not push real operations out of view.

parameters.name: since
parameters.description: version of the change list the caller last read.

get.description: List the owner's saved Change Cards for this project, most recently saved first, with each card's summary, status, the request_revision in force, the request_revision of a revision the guide proposed beside a confirmed card while it waits for the user, the state of its most recently accepted verification run and whether its revision and selected tests are current, and when it was last saved, and say whether this server can record approvals. The views page opens on this list; agents use it to find a change_id. Reading changes nothing.

403.description: forbidden: The authenticated caller may not perform this operation or does not own the resource.

post.description: Record Checkpoint 5 approval for the owner's confirmed Change Card revision. The control plane chooses the tests' commit the same way verify_change does (the suite commit in the project's stored verification settings, or the tests Surla accepted for the change's build at request_revision), loads the verification report by digest, re-derives the report from its evidence with verify.Approve, and records the approval on the card when the report passed for candidate_commit, request_revision, and that tests' commit. When promotion settings are configured with surla promotion set (or a PromotionTarget is bound), approve_merge also checks that the staged binaries in <release_dir>/<candidate_commit>/ match the report's binary digests and records those digests in artifacts; without promotion settings, no release folder or staged binaries are required and artifacts is empty. The report's suite_id and environment are what the tests at suite_commit declared and are recorded on the approval without a separate comparison. Nothing is merged or deployed. It checks again, with git, that the candidate is on the build's branch, descends from its base and holds no other build's work.

404.description: not_found: No Change Card exists with this change_id.

409.description:
build_branch_mismatch: The run's candidate is no longer on the build's branch, or that branch now holds another build's work: the builder verifies again, then the user approves that run.

conflict: The Change Card is not confirmed, its request_revision does not match, or the accepted tests changed while approving; confirm the card, read the current revision with get_change, or approve again.

no_build: Without stored verification settings: the user has not built the change's revision in force with a test writer, so no tests are accepted for it. The message names the revision built, if any, and ends with the user's step.

tests_not_accepted: Without stored verification settings: Surla has not accepted the tests of the change's build. The message names the test writer's state and who acts, and ends with the step.

422.description: unprocessable: The verification report did not pass or does not match the Change Card, the chosen tests' commit, or (when promotion settings are configured) the promotion target's staged binary digests.

501.description: not_implemented: This control plane has no verification configuration bound to it.

post.description: Confirm or refine a Checkpoint 1 Change Card with the complete ambiguity answers and example table, or adopt the revision the guide proposed beside a confirmed card. Only the user's browser session calls it, from the views page; the guide revises with revise_change and never confirms. Naming the proposed revision's request_revision adopts it: its questions are answered, it becomes the confirmed revision in force under a new request_revision with no approval, and the proposal is gone. While a proposal waits, refining the confirmed revision is refused: adopt or decline the proposal first. Otherwise the request names the card's request_revision: changed answers or examples produce a new request_revision; unchanged ones return the card as it is, with a saved approval returned in approval only while its suite_commit is still the tests' commit chosen for this revision and either no promotion target is configured or its binary digests still match the promotion target's current binaries, or in unverified_approval when a promotion target is configured and cannot measure the candidate's binaries. A decision that no option expresses goes to the guide, which records it with revise_change; the user then confirms the resulting revision.

409.description: conflict: request_revision names neither the card's revision nor a waiting proposal's, or it names the confirmed revision while a proposal waits (adopt or decline the proposal first); read the change with get_change.

422.description: unprocessable: The submitted answers or examples did not satisfy the Change Card's requirements; the message states which check failed.

post.description: Decline the revision the guide proposed beside a confirmed Checkpoint 1 Change Card. The proposal is removed and the confirmed revision in force stays exactly as it was, with its answers, confirmation, approval, Stories and design source. Only the user may decline; the guide replaces a proposal by revising again. The result is the change as get_change returns it.

409.description: conflict: No proposed revision waits, or request_revision does not name it; read the change with get_change.

post.description: Return the Checkpoint 2 C4 container topology, tool contracts, and Goa-AI guardrails of a confirmed Change Card's agreed revision, from the architecture its refresh evaluated and the revision saved; it reads and evaluates no file. It refuses a design with no Goa API or Service container and an agent without positive TimeBudget and DefaultCaps(MaxToolCalls). The result reports what the design declares; it does not compare the design with the Change Card's requirements. The guide sees the architecture of an unsaved draft with surla preview -dir <draft_folder>.

404.description: not_found: No Change Card exists with this change_id.

409.description: conflict: The Change Card is not confirmed, its request_revision does not match, or the agreed revision records no architecture to show; confirm the card or read the current revision with get_change.

422.description: unprocessable: The request or evaluated design did not meet Checkpoint 2 requirements; the message states which check failed.

post.description: Save a new Checkpoint 1 Change Card from a feature request and the caller's analysis of it. Surla checks the analysis's structure and cross-field rules, gives ambiguities the IDs <change_id>-ambiguity-NN and examples the IDs check_01, check_02, ... in list order, binds the card to the authenticated owner, and computes request_revision. With story_refresh_op_id, Surla saves what that succeeded refresh_story operation evaluated: the draft's design, Stories, architecture, go.mod and made-from list; it reads no file. A project with a go.mod requires story_refresh_op_id for a new card; with neither a go.mod nor an op_id, the card records no design. An op_id whose refresh read the draft before the user dropped a build is refused with drafted_before_drop. Every card waits for user confirmation, including a card without ambiguities. Surla runs no model for this step and cannot judge whether the analysis is complete or correct.

409.description:
drafted_before_drop: A build was dropped after this refresh. Call refresh_story to remake and evaluate the draft.

conflict: A Change Card with this change_id already exists; use revise_change or a new change_id.

422.description: unprocessable: The request could not be accepted: change_id or prompt is blank, an ambiguity repeats an option, story_refresh_op_id does not name the owner's current succeeded refresh_story operation, or the project folder holds a go.mod and story_refresh_op_id is missing. The message says which; nothing was saved.

post.description: Save the next revision of an existing Checkpoint 1 Change Card from a revised feature request and the guide's analysis of it. Only the guide revises a change; only the user confirms or adopts a revision, with confirm_intent on the views page. The request is bound to the latest revision: the proposed revision's request_revision when one waits, otherwise the card's. On a card that was never confirmed, the new revision replaces it. On a confirmed card, the new revision is saved as the proposed revision beside the confirmed one, replacing any earlier proposal, and the confirmed revision stays in force with its answers, confirmation, approval, Stories and design source until the user adopts the proposal with confirm_intent or declines it. The analysis accounts for every example of the revision it revises exactly once, keeping or editing it through prior_id or dropping it through removed_example_ids. Surla keeps the IDs of kept examples, gives new examples the lowest check_NN ID neither card uses, adopts the evaluated draft's design, Stories, architecture, go.mod and made-from list when story_refresh_op_id is given, without reading any file, or keeps every snapshot field of the revision it revises when it is omitted, even with zero Stories, and saves the new revision in needs_confirmation status for the user's review. The new revision has no answers, confirmed_by or approval: earlier decisions carry over only where the analysis restates them in its summary, examples or preserved behaviors. The result is the change as get_change returns it. Surla runs no model for this step and cannot judge whether the analysis is complete or correct. A project with a go.mod refuses an omitted op_id when the revision being revised has no design. A refresh from before the user dropped a build is refused with drafted_before_drop.

The message says which; the card did not change.

get.description: Return the current Change Card, including its request_revision, to its owner, for example after confirm_intent or revise_change refused an edit made against an older revision. The card's fields describe the revision in force; a revision the guide proposed beside a confirmed card is returned in proposed_revision while it waits. Reading never confirms or changes the card. A recorded approval is returned in approval only while its suite_commit is still the tests' commit chosen for this revision and either no promotion target is configured or its binary digests still match the promotion target's current binaries, or in unverified_approval when a promotion target is configured and cannot measure the candidate's binaries.

get.description: Return a change's build when it is the project's open build, with whether the user has taken it: building, passed with the commits to merge, merged, or dropped. not_started when it is not, including a builder-only build whose stored verification settings were removed; start a new build on the views page. Otherwise return the revision built, when, whether each role read its assignment, the test writer's state with the number of Surla's findings (never their text), and whether the build is for the change's revision in force. Reading changes nothing; deciding merged reads the project's repository.

404.description: not_found: No Change Card exists with this change_id.

post.description: The user starts building a confirmed change at its agreed revision, the one in force, on the project owner's bound team. A project has one open build. Building another change is refused with previous_change_open until the user has merged a passed run of the open build into the branch checked out in the project folder or dropped it with drop_build. Building the open build's own change again keeps its number and base and replaces its assignments; while no verification of it has passed, replaces must name the open build the page showed, else unfinished_build_open; once that build is merged or dropped, building its change again starts a new build. Surla first checks, without effects, merge or drop, a revision drafted before a drop, and the agreed design against the project's commit; numbers a new build one more than any surla/build-<n> or surla/tests-<n> branch and the open build; and saves it with its base, the project's commit, by one rename. Then it makes a missing working copy (.surla-build, and .surla-tests when a test writer is used) on the build's own branch and registers the builder and the test writer in their copies. Build moves no existing copy: each joins the build's branch when its worker first reads the assignment. A refused start saves nothing; after the save, a server stop leaves the build saved, and building again makes a missing copy and registers the roles. After the start's turns are released, bringing the team up has its own 45-second limit. get_build reads the saved build without this start's transient team outcome.

403.description: forbidden: The authenticated caller may not perform this operation or does not own the resource.

404.description: not_found: No Change Card exists with this change_id.

409.description:
conflict: The Change Card is not confirmed or request_revision is not its agreed revision (a waiting proposal's revision cannot be built), or the agreed revision records no design to build from; nothing changed.

not_repository: The project folder is not in a Git repository, which every build's working copies need; nothing was saved. The message ends with the step to create or select a repository.

no_commit: The project repository has no commit for the build's working copies to start from; nothing was saved. The message ends with the step to make its first commit.

no_test_layout: This project has neither stored verification settings nor Surla's test layout; nothing was saved. Store verification settings, then build again.

git_identity_missing: Git has no configured name and address, which Surla uses to commit what a working copy left when it joins a new build and to record accepted tests; nothing was saved. Configure Git's name and address, then build again.

copy_folder_in_use: A working copy's folder in the project folder, .surla-build or .surla-tests, is a file or a folder that is not a linked working copy of the project's repository; nothing was saved. The message names the folder and ends with the step to move it out of the project.

tests_branch_in_use: The branch Surla checks out in a missing working copy, surla/build-<n> or surla/tests-<n>, is checked out in another folder; nothing was saved. The message names that folder, quoted, and ends with the step that frees the branch.

working_copy_busy: Another build is starting, a worker is reading its assignment into its working copy, or a test check holds the test writer's working copy; nothing was saved. Start the build again when that has ended.

previous_change_open: Another change's build is open, and the user has neither merged a passed run of it into the branch checked out in the project folder nor dropped it; nothing was saved. The body names that build, with the commits to merge once a run passed, so the page offers the merge commands and Drop.

unfinished_build_open: Building this change again replaces its open build, which no verification has passed, and replaces does not name that build; nothing was saved. The page asks the user first, then sends replaces naming the build it showed.

drafted_before_drop: The agreed revision was drafted before the user dropped another change, so its design can hold that change's design; nothing was saved. The guide revises the change from its draft; the user adopts the revision, then builds.

design_changed_outside: A design file at the build's base commit is not a version the agreed revision was made from: it was changed outside Surla; nothing was saved. The message names the file and the commit. When the change is uncommitted, commit the design change in the project folder first; then the guide calls update_draft, refresh_story and revise_change, and the user adopts the revision and builds.

422.description: unprocessable: The agreed Story has a finished flow whose key gives its required test an empty name, or two finished flows whose required tests would have the same name; revise the Story. Nothing changed.

501.description: not_implemented: Start this project with surla to bind the team; nothing was saved.

503.description: unavailable: The server is stopping or the start's time limit ended before saving; call again on a running server. Nothing was saved.

post.description: The user drops the project's open build on the views page because the change will not be taken: Surla builds nothing on it, and it no longer blocks starting another build. A change whose agreed revision was drafted before the drop is still refused with drafted_before_drop, which get_build's drafted_before_drop reports, until the guide refreshes the draft and revises the change and the user adopts the revision. The request names the build the page showed; a different open build (a second tab built or dropped meanwhile) is refused with its facts, and a build already dropped is refused. Drop writes one record, the start of the guide's made-from list naming the dropped build, by one rename: its only write. It changes no working copy, branch, draft or file of the user's: the build's commits stay on its branches, and the guide's next refresh_story makes the draft again from the project folder. From then on no role has work for the build, and the builder's and the test writer's tools tell them it was dropped. A merged build may be dropped too. The result is the dropped build as get_build reports it.

A build whose tests do not need changes is refused. Reading changes nothing.

get.description: Return all Checkpoint 4 verification runs started by the owner for a Change Card, ordered newest first by accepted_at (tie-broken by run_id), with each run's current state, the Change Card revision it was started for and where its tests came from. Works whether the Change Card is currently confirmed or in needs_confirmation after a later revision. The test writer lists only the runs of a change it has an assignment for.

post.description: Start Checkpoint 4 verification of a candidate commit for the owner's confirmed Change Card revision and return its run_id at once. The change's build must be the project's open build, not dropped, and the builder's working copy must have joined it. Before any run Surla checks, with git in the project's repository: the candidate is on the build's branch surla/build-<n>, descends from the build's base and is not that base, and holds no commit of another build's branch that the base lacks; its design/ files, read by the design walk in gofmt form, are the build's design source version for version; and every design version at its merge base with the project's commit is one the revision was made from. With verification settings stored with surla verification set, the run uses the operator's evaluator. Otherwise Surla must have accepted the build's tests: the run builds the candidate's programs from the candidate commit and runs the generated entry point of the tests at the accepted commit. The server builds the commit and runs the tests in a separate process that keeps running when the caller disconnects or the server restarts; the builds, the tests and the programs they start run as ordinary processes with the user's file and network access. get_verification reads its state. Only the builder view of the report is ever returned, with where its tests came from. A candidate the user already merged still verifies.

404.description: not_found: No Change Card exists with this change_id.

409.description:
assignment_unread: A build started after your last read of your assignment: stop your current work, then call get_builder_assignment for its change.

copy_off_branch: Your working copy is not on the build's branch: the message states its branch, the build's branch and what is uncommitted, and the goal. Put your work there with git, commit it, and verify again.

working_folder_missing: Your working folder is missing; ask the user to build this change again on the views page.

build_branch_mismatch: The candidate is not on your build's branch, does not descend from the build's base, is the base itself, or holds a commit of another build's branch that the base lacks. The message names the commit and, for another build's work, its branch and the files it changed, and states the goal: your branch and working copy hold none of that work.

design_changed_outside: A design file at the candidate's merge base with the project's commit is not a version the revision was made from: it was changed outside Surla. The message names the file and the commit. When the change is uncommitted, the user commits the design change in the project folder, then asks the guide to call update_draft, refresh_story and revise_change.

conflict: The Change Card is not confirmed or its request_revision does not match, the candidate commit is not in the project's repository, the project folder was replaced after the server started, the candidate's design/ files differ from the build's design source (the message names them; call generate_code, commit and verify again), or (without stored verification settings) the candidate changes hand-written files in the test module.

no_build: No build of this change is open (the user built another change or none), the user dropped it, or the open build is for another revision of the change. The message names what Surla found and the user's step.

tests_not_accepted: Without stored verification settings: Surla has not accepted the tests of the change's build. The message names the test writer's state and who acts, and ends with the step.

no_test_layout: Without stored verification settings: a commit lacks the test layout surla init makes, the accepted tests' commit is no longer in the project's repository, or the project folder is not in a git repository. The message names the commit or folder and what is missing, and ends with the step.

501.description: not_implemented: This server has no verification configuration, so it cannot run Checkpoint 4 verifications.

get.description: Report the model choice live targets started afterwards receive: none, a direct provider and model name, or a model gateway address. It starts as none. While no model is chosen, a hand_over_model_settings call that holds a provider's settings selects that provider's default model; every accepted configure_model call replaces the choice. It never returns an API key or any other setting value, and it changes nothing. Verification runs do not use this choice.

403.description: forbidden: The authenticated caller may not perform this operation or does not own the resource.

post.description: Choose, on a running control plane without restarting, the model that CP3 live targets started afterwards receive: a direct provider and model name, whose request settings the surla command handed to the project server with hand_over_model_settings, or a running gRPC model gateway. With written tests, a direct provider is served by the executor's loopback model gateway and the accepted test program receives only that gateway, never provider settings. The executor-owned gateway has no authentication: any local process, including another user's, can use it while the target runs without receiving the provider key. With stored verification settings, the evaluator receives the choice and its chosen provider's settings. A configured gateway is passed through unchanged.

403.description: forbidden: The authenticated caller may not perform this operation or does not own the resource.

422.description: unprocessable: The field combination is invalid, or the project server holds no request settings for the chosen provider; the message names the provider's key variable and how to hand it over.

post.description: The surla command, after it confirms the project server's identity, hands over the request settings of each model provider whose key is set in the shell it runs in: the key and the listed settings that route and authenticate the provider's requests. The project server holds them in memory only and forgets them when it stops. A live target using stored verification settings receives the chosen provider's held settings; a verification with that evaluator receives every held provider's settings. Accepted written tests receive no provider settings in verification or live targets: for a direct live model the executor serves an executor-owned loopback model gateway. It has no authentication: any local process, including another user's, can use it while the target runs without receiving the provider key. The check helper receives none. An absent provider attribute keeps what is held for that provider. A present one replaces everything held for it and must include the provider's key variable; an empty one is refused, because it is neither a way to keep nor a way to forget. A request with neither attribute changes nothing and reports what is held. When no model is chosen and a provider is now held, live targets use that provider's default model, anthropic before openai; any other choice stays. The result names the held variables and the model choice, never a value. Only the surla command's management credential may call this operation; it is never an MCP tool.

Otherwise the change's current revision must have a build with accepted tests: the candidate programs come from candidate_commit and the test program from the accepted tests commit. Written tests require a chosen model; with a direct provider the executor serves an executor-owned loopback model gateway and passes no provider setting to the program. Return bounded safe summaries newest first, without reading the entire file. Older pages and later refreshes work on the same running server and after restart. Recording is automatic in the project server. Authenticated HTTP/MCP domain calls have a surla.request.<operation> boundary span, with child domain operations recorded separately. Reads by the user's views page that succeed or are refused (sent with GET, such as the reads the page repeats whenever the project changes) are exported but not added to this private history; such a read that ends with an error status or a panic is added. Waiting reads are never added, whoever sends them; every other agent call and every operation that changes something is added. Requests rejected before authentication or decoding and separate verification processes are absent.

post.description: The guide brings design changes made outside Surla into its draft, before drafting a new change and when told a design file changed in the project folder. Under the draft's lock Surla compares each design file's draft and live versions over a recorded base. The history base is the latest recorded version present in the project's committed history since the draft's start, or the starting folder version when that history supplies none. The comparison base is whichever of that history base and the outside version the draft last took was recorded later; with no previous take, it is the history base. A live version equal to the comparison base brings nothing. If the project's committed history gained a recorded version since the last take, Surla takes and reports the live version without merging it. Otherwise an outside change is taken when the draft did not change that file, merged with git merge-file when both changed it, and listed to correct when both changed the same lines or one side removed what the other changed. A draft file Go cannot parse, and a module the project's go.mod requires at another version or with another replace directive than the draft's, are listed to correct; Surla does not merge go.mod. Each listed file names the folder that holds it: the guide corrects a file of its draft, while a design file or go.mod of the project folder that cannot be parsed is the user's to correct there and the guide never edits it. When the project's commit, the draft, the project's files or the draft's made-from list change while Surla prepares the update, Surla brings nothing and answers conflict, and the guide calls update_draft again. Surla records an interrupted update so a later call can finish it without merging its result again; if the guide changed the file in between, the file is listed to correct. An uncommitted revert to an older version may bring nothing; when a build reports design_changed_outside for an uncommitted design change, the user commits the change in the project folder, then asks the guide to call update_draft, refresh_story and revise_change. Otherwise call refresh_story after this update. Takes no input.

post.description: Write the open build's agreed design into the builder's working folder and regenerate its code. Surla replaces, creates or removes the Go files under the builder's design/ so that design/ holds exactly the build's design source (never a test file or testdata; a linked design/ is refused), then compares each module the design imports with the go.mod the revision was made from: when the builder's go.mod lacks a module or requires an older version, the call names go get <module>@<version> and go mod tidy, prefixed GOWORK=off when the assignment's gowork_off is true, writes design/ and generates nothing until they are run. A differing replace directive for a module the design imports is also named, including the saved replacement line or the fact that none was saved, so the builder corrects go.mod before calling again. Otherwise it compiles and runs the design as an ordinary process with the user's file and network access and atomically replaces gen/, preserving top-level user files and leaving go.mod and go.sum unchanged. With target eval it regenerates the working folder's eval/ module from its own design. Return the written paths and warnings; a warning after gen/ publication still means generation succeeded. It compiles the design only; it does not build the application or run tests.

CP1Analysis.title: CP1Analysis

ambiguities.description: Open questions only the requester can answer: product, domain, or operational choices that change observable behavior or service boundaries. Do not ask about details the request or the design already settle; state them in summary, or in examples when they change an observable outcome. Send an empty list when nothing is open.

examples.description: Concrete acceptance examples drawn from the request and the design, never placeholder text; each becomes a check the change must pass.

preserved_behaviors.description: Existing behaviors and contract rules of the target that the change must keep, each stated concretely; empty when none apply.

summary.description: Plain-English description of the requested behavior, including the details the request or the design already settle.

ui_composition.description: Optional OpenUI Lang program that helps the requester decide the open questions, built only from the decision components the surla://golden-path resource lists. Refer to an ambiguity or example only by its 1-based position in this analysis (1 is the first); never invent identifiers. Surla saves it unchanged without checking it; the views page validates and renders it. Omit it when a plain card is clearer.

CP1Analysis.description: Your analysis of the feature request against the target's current Goa design (its design/*.go files) and the Golden Path playbook served at surla://golden-path. Surla saves it as the Change Card after checking its structure and cross-field rules; it cannot judge whether the analysis is complete or correct.

CP1AnalysisAmbiguity.title: CP1AnalysisAmbiguity

options.description: At least two distinct, self-contained choices; each states the behavior it selects and what follows from it. The requester's answer must be exactly one of these strings.

question.description: The decision in plain language, saying what the choice changes.

CP1AnalysisAmbiguity.description: One product, domain, or operational choice only the requester can make. Surla gives it the ID <change_id>-ambiguity-NN, numbered in list order.

CP1AnalysisExample.title: CP1AnalysisExample

expected_outcome.description: The observable result or refusal that must hold.

input_summary.description: The actual request, inputs, and starting state in this scenario, with real values from the request and the design, never placeholders.

scenario.description: Short name of the situation, in the requester's domain terms.

verification_kind.description: deterministic when code can check the outcome directly; model_judged when checking it needs judgment.

CP1AnalysisExample.description: One concrete acceptance example that becomes a check the change must pass. Surla gives it the ID check_01, check_02, ... in list order.

CP1RevisionAnalysis.title: CP1RevisionAnalysis

ambiguities.description: Open questions only the requester can answer: product, domain, or operational choices that change observable behavior or service boundaries. Do not ask about details the request, the design or a confirmed answer already settle; state them in summary, or in examples when they change an observable outcome. Send an empty list when nothing is open.

examples.description: Concrete acceptance examples drawn from the revised request and the design. Give prior_id for each current example you keep or edit; omit it for new ones.

preserved_behaviors.description: Existing behaviors and contract rules of the target that the change must keep, each stated concretely; empty when none apply.

items.example: swo

removed_example_ids.description: IDs of the current card's examples this revision drops. Every current example ID appears exactly once, either as an examples[].prior_id or here; send an empty list when none are dropped.

summary.description: Plain-English description of the revised behavior, including the details the request, the design or confirmed answers already settle.

ui_composition.description: Optional OpenUI Lang program that helps the requester decide the open questions, built only from the decision components the surla://golden-path resource lists. Refer to an ambiguity or example only by its 1-based position in this analysis (1 is the first); never invent identifiers. Surla saves it unchanged without checking it; the views page validates and renders it. Omit it when a plain card is clearer.

CP1RevisionAnalysis.description: Your analysis of the revised request against the current Change Card (as get_change returns it at request_revision), the target's current Goa design, and the Golden Path playbook served at surla://golden-path. A confirmed answer stays settled unless the revised request or design contradicts it: do not ask it again, and restate it in summary, examples or preserved_behaviors, because the revised card drops every answer. An explicit instruction in the revised request or design replaces the decisions, examples and preserved behaviors it affects. An unanswered question stays in ambiguities unless the revised request or design answers it or removes its scope. Everything else on the current card stays unless the revised request or design changes it. Surla checks the structure and the example accounting; it cannot judge whether the analysis is complete or correct.

DraftCorrection.title: DraftCorrection

folder.description: Which folder holds the file to correct: draft_folder is the guide's draft, at the result's draft_folder; project_folder is the user's project folder, which holds the draft.

path.description: Path relative to the folder that folder names, such as design/types.go or go.mod.

problem.description: What to correct. In the draft: conflict markers where the draft and the project folder changed the same lines; a file removed on one side and changed on the other; a draft file Go cannot parse, with its line; a file whose project change Surla took without merging, or was writing when it stopped, to check that it holds the intended edits once; or a module the project's go.mod requires at another version than the draft's, or that the draft's lacks, including differing replace directives and a differing module path. In the project folder: a design file or go.mod there that cannot be parsed, with its line, or a go.mod that declares no module.

DraftCorrection.description: A file to correct before update_draft can bring a change forward, and the folder that holds it. When folder is draft_folder, the guide corrects the file in its draft. When folder is project_folder, the file is the user's own, in the project folder: the guide tells the user what to correct there and waits, and never edits it. The guide calls update_draft again until none is listed, then refresh_story.

ProposedRevisionItem.description: A revision the guide proposed with revise_change beside the confirmed revision in force. It waits until the user adopts it, by answering its questions and confirming its request_revision with confirm_intent, or declines it with decline_revision. Until then the confirmed revision stays in force with its answers, confirmation, approval, Stories and design source, and architecture preview, verification and approval keep working on it. A later revise_change naming this request_revision replaces it.

working_folder.description: Folder to write the tests in: your own working copy of the project, .surla-tests, on the build's branch surla/tests-<n>. Do not commit there: Surla commits what it accepts.

TestWriterAssignment.description: The test writer's assignment for one build: write the required tests for the Story as agreed at the built revision, in the test module (eval/) of the working folder, and make them hold the service to the user's confirmed answers, confirmation examples and preserved behaviors of that revision, which the assignment carries exactly as confirmed. Surla writes eval/design/story_tests.go, which declares the required tests, from the agreed Story and generates the module at each read that marks the assignment read and again at each report; the test writer leaves that file as it is. After changing the module's design, the test writer reports to have it generated again or runs surla gen -dir eval in the working folder first; regenerating keeps the required tests. go build ./... in eval/ checks the work before a report, and Surla's check of each report is the judge.

suite_commit.description: Commit of the tests the run uses: the operator's evaluator, or the tests accepted for the change's build.

test_source.description: Where the run's tests came from, recorded when the run started: evaluator, or written_tests with their commit and a notice.

commit.description: Commit Surla recorded the accepted tests at; the same as suite_commit.

notice.description: Always: These tests were written by a separate agent on this machine and are not isolated from the builder.
notice.example: Accusantium rerum error quam ab et.

VerificationStatusResult.description: One Checkpoint 4 verification run of a candidate commit for a confirmed Change Card revision, and its current state. The run keeps the revision it was started for, so a later confirm_intent does not change it.

example.candidate_commit: Molestiae totam nam nobis quidem reprehenderit quae.

candidate_commit.description: Full commit ID of the candidate to build and verify (40 or 64 lowercase hex characters).

request_revision.description: Current request_revision of the confirmed Change Card.
